name: Huayhuash Circuit Trek
summary: A full loop of the Cordillera Huayhuash, around 120–135 km of camping at altitude with a dozen passes above 4,500 m, several of them close to 5,000 m. Shorter eight-day versions cut part of the eastern side; the full circuit takes about twelve.

name: Santa Cruz Trek
summary: The best-known walk in Huascarán National Park, about 50 km between Cashapampa and Vaquería linking two valleys over the Punta Unión pass. Short and non-technical, but the pass is high enough that acclimatisation in Huaraz first matters.

name: Alpamayo Circuit Trek
summary: A long loop through the northern Cordillera Blanca that circles Alpamayo, usually starting at Hualcayán and crossing a run of passes between 4,600 m and 4,850 m. Most days are spent above 4,000 m, camping, with little resupply on the way.

name: Cedros–Alpamayo Traverse
summary: The point-to-point version of the Alpamayo route, normally Hualcayán to Cashapampa or Vaquería via the Cedros valley and the north-west face of Alpamayo, about 96 km in nine days. It shares its last section with the Santa Cruz trek.

name: Colca Canyon Trek
summary: A descent from the canyon rim at Cabanaconde to the villages and the Sangalle oasis on the floor, then back up the same 1,200 m of height. The route only loses altitude, but the climb out is done in one hot morning and is what people find hard.

name: Cotahuasi Canyon Trek
summary: A walk down one of the deepest canyons in the world, in Arequipa's far north-west, past the Sipia falls to Chaupo, Velinga and Quechualla at under 2,000 m. Itineraries vary widely in where they start and how far down-canyon they go.
